metadata.title: Advisory Attack Response Recommendation Layer Evaluation
metadata.architecture: Hierarchical Two-Stage Classification with Downstream Advisory Response Mapping

Normal.recommended_action: No immediate defensive intervention required. Maintain continuous telemetry collection and routine anomaly-detection baseline updates.
Normal.operator_guidance: Continue standard baseline monitoring. Audit periodic false-negative rates and ensure logging infrastructure operates without dropped packets.
Normal.rationale: Flow statistical features correspond to established non-malicious baseline communication profiles within the evaluated network topology.
Normal.limitations: Advisory classification. Normal attribution does not guarantee the complete absence of subtle, stealthy, or novel evasion techniques (Stage 1 false-negative rate is 13.18%).

Analysis.recommended_action: Inspect unusual protocol and port-probing behavior. Correlate with firewall and DNS query telemetry, and review potential reconnaissance or port-scan indicators.
Analysis.operator_guidance: Review originating host IP connection patterns, port sweep frequencies, protocol header anomalies, and correlation with known vulnerability-scanning tools.
Analysis.rationale: Analysis-classified traffic typically reflects automated vulnerability scanning, port probing, or protocol fingerprinting preceding active intrusion attempts.
Analysis.limitations: Advisory only. Stage 2 multiclass classification demonstrates acute minority-class limitations for Analysis (2.95% end-to-end recall). Misclassifications with benign administration traffic or other probe types are frequent.

Backdoor.recommended_action: Investigate unexpected persistence or remote-access mechanisms on the target endpoint. Review authentication logs, unusual process creation, and recent system configuration changes.
Backdoor.operator_guidance: Examine endpoint process trees, listening sockets, outbound reverse-shell connections, and user logon records for the destination host.
Backdoor.rationale: Backdoor traffic characteristics indicate covert remote administrative channels, reverse TCP tunnels, or unauthorized persistent access mechanisms.
Backdoor.limitations: Advisory only. Stage 2 exhibits substantial confusion between Backdoor instances and DoS/Exploits (11.57% end-to-end recall). Manual endpoint telemetry verification is required prior to concluding host compromise.

DoS.recommended_action: Inspect traffic volume and connection-rate anomalies. Consider operator-approved rate limiting, connection throttling, or upstream packet filtering, while actively monitoring service availability.
DoS.operator_guidance: Review source IP distribution, TCP SYN or UDP flood characteristics, interface queue depths, and application response latencies on the target server.
DoS.rationale: Denial-of-Service flow characteristics reflect high-frequency packet transmission aimed at exhaustively consuming network bandwidth, socket tables, or CPU resources.
DoS.limitations: Advisory only. Legitimate traffic spikes (flash crowds) or transient network congestion can match DoS statistical signatures. Does not independently prove malicious intent.

Exploits.recommended_action: Inspect targeted application and daemon service logs. Review known vulnerability and patch status, and investigate suspicious payload or malformed request patterns.
Exploits.operator_guidance: Correlate payload signatures with CVE advisories, inspect web server and database query logs for injection or buffer-overflow attempts, and verify application integrity.
Exploits.rationale: Exploit traffic exhibits structural or payload traits consistent with weaponized attempts to compromise known software vulnerabilities in exposed network services.
Exploits.limitations: Advisory only. Does not confirm that an exploit payload succeeded or that the target service was vulnerable. Stage 2 achieved 53.78% end-to-end recall on Exploits.

Fuzzers.recommended_action: Inspect malformed or out-of-specification request patterns. Review application parser error logs, and consider input-validation hardening and rate-limiting controls.
Fuzzers.operator_guidance: Check application crash telemetry, exception logs, protocol syntax violations, and high-frequency parameter mutation sequences directed at input handlers.
Fuzzers.rationale: Fuzzing involves injecting semi-random, boundary-condition, or malformed data streams to trigger software faults or identify unhandled parsing exceptions.
Fuzzers.limitations: Advisory only. Stage 1 has a severe false-negative filtering bottleneck on Fuzzers (74.35% missed at Stage 1, yielding 14.83% end-to-end recall). Flows reaching this recommendation represent only a fraction of true fuzzing attempts.

Generic.recommended_action: Perform secondary incident triage. Correlate network flow evidence with endpoint and security information logs, and investigate source and destination operational context.
Generic.operator_guidance: Review cryptographic protocol consistency, destination IP reputation scores, and traffic volume against baseline profiles to identify the specific threat vector.
Generic.rationale: Generic classifications capture cryptographic block-cipher collisions and generalized signature matches across broad attack templates.
Generic.limitations: Advisory only. Generic serves as a broad umbrella classification (98.06% end-to-end recall), meaning secondary investigation is necessary to determine the precise underlying attack type.

Reconnaissance.recommended_action: Inspect scanning and sweep activity. Review source IP behavior across multiple destination ports and services, and evaluate network perimeter monitoring policies.
Reconnaissance.operator_guidance: Analyze horizontal port sweeps, ICMP ping sweeps, banner grabbing attempts, and firewall drop counters associated with the originating IP address.
Reconnaissance.rationale: Reconnaissance traffic seeks to map network topology, active host addresses, and listening service versions to prepare for targeted secondary intrusion attempts.
Reconnaissance.limitations: Advisory only. Authorized network administration tasks, internal asset inventory scanners, and monitoring probes produce flow profiles identical to malicious reconnaissance.

Shellcode.recommended_action: Inspect endpoint process, memory, and host-level security telemetry. Investigate possible code-execution payloads, and review affected service binary and memory integrity.
Shellcode.operator_guidance: Examine memory execution logs, abnormal child processes spawned by network services, in-memory payload staging, and outbound command-and-control beacons.
Shellcode.rationale: Shellcode traffic carries compact machine-code instructions intended to hijack program control flow and spawn an interactive command shell upon exploitation.
Shellcode.limitations: Advisory only. Shellcode achieved 63.46% end-to-end recall in the benchmark evaluation. The recommendation does not confirm that memory execution occurred or that the target host was successfully compromised.

Worms.recommended_action: Investigate possible lateral propagation across network nodes. Inspect east-west communication patterns, and evaluate network segmentation and containment options with human authorization.
Worms.operator_guidance: Audit internal lateral traffic for uniform scanning and payload replication patterns, inspect adjacent subnet activity, and verify endpoint patch levels for wormable vulnerabilities.
Worms.rationale: Worms self-propagate autonomously across network vulnerabilities, posing immediate compounding risk to interconnected IoT devices and internal subnets.
Worms.limitations: Advisory only. The underlying UNSW-NB15 training distribution contained only 130 Worms instances, creating high classification uncertainty (15.38% end-to-end recall). Requires rapid human validation.

safety_and_boundaries.statement: The evaluated advisory response recommendation layer maps predicted categories to static, structured guidance objects. It implements zero automated remediation, executes zero system or firewall commands, and introduces zero per-flow blockchain calls.

limitations: Recommendation quality is strictly bounded by upstream classification accuracy.
15,730 true attack flows (primarily Fuzzers) misclassified as Normal receive benign monitoring guidance.
1,282 true benign flows misclassified by Stage 1 receive false-alarm attack investigation guidance.
Minority classes (Analysis: 2.95% recall, Worms: 15.38% recall) produce limited and uncertain recommendations.
Advisory nature requires manual human validation prior to initiating any defensive intervention.
